 Report now Ajeti's Reunion with His Former Club 
 "More Basel German is spoken in the Lugano locker room than at FCB."
 Albian Ajeti has regained his top form in Lugano.
 KEYSTONE
 Albian Ajeti found himself on the bench at FC Basel. Now he’s back in top form with Super League leader Lugano. On Sunday, he’ll face his former teammates in a big reunion.
 Jan Arnet 
 Today at 11:58 Here's what it's all about
 After finding himself on the bench at FC Basel, Albian Ajeti joined FC Lugano on loan this summer.
 The change of scenery seems to have done the forward good. In Ticino, Ajeti is scoring goals regularly again.
 This Sunday, Lugano and Basel will face off (4:30 p.m., live on blue Sport). FCB coach Jokanovic says of Ajeti: “He’ll certainly be extra motivated.”
 Summary created with Albian Ajeti is on fire again! The player who, two years ago, was one of the key contributors to FC Basel’s double victory with 12 goals and 9 assists, has regained his top form. He has scored 6 goals in 9 games for FC Lugano—the forward is even more efficient now than he was during FC Basel’s championship season of 24/25.
 Last season, Ajeti scored just 5 goals in 45 games for FCB. The change of scenery seems to have done the Basel native good. That said, if you ask Ajeti, FC Lugano is more “Basel-like” than Basel itself. “More Basel German is spoken in the Lugano locker room than at FCB,” he said recently in an interview with the “Basler Zeitung” . With Uran Bislimi, backup goalie Felix Gebhardt, and youngster Gjan Ajdin, three other former FCB youth players are now playing in Ticino.
 In this interview, Ajeti also spoke candidly about his difficult situation at the Joggeli and his loan move to Lugano. “The whole situation surrounding FC Basel hurt me,” he said. After a difficult previous season, he wanted to show everyone what he was still capable of. “But then I wasn’t allowed to do that anymore.”
 No Trust Left in Basel
 Ajeti was no longer playing any role at all under Stephan Lichtsteiner and ended up in the stands. Then the offer came from Lugano—and the 29-year-old accepted. “Also because not many people at FC Basel tried to talk me out of making the move,” he says. “The decision to go to Lugano was made easy for me. I didn’t hear anything from President David Degen. Toward the end, I no longer felt any trust in Basel.”
 On Sunday, Ajeti will be reunited with his former teammates, whose season is still not going as hoped and who now have a new coach, Slavisa Jokanovic, on the sidelines. “I’m sure Ajeti will be extra motivated,” Jokanovic says of Ajeti. “Wanting to get one over on your former club in this situation is completely normal.”
